questions.question:
Assertion(A): When an apple of mass 'm' falls from a tree of height 'h', the kinetic energy will be less than 'mgh' on reaching the ground.
Reason(R): The conservation of mechanical energy is strictly valid only in the absence of friction due to air.

options.a: Both assertion and reason are true.
options.b: Both assertion and reason are false.
options.c: Assertion is false but reason is true.
options.d: Assertion is true but reason is false.

questions.solution: (a) Both assertion and reason are true. Part of the potential energy mgh is used against air friction, so KE on reaching the ground is less than mgh; mechanical energy is conserved only when there is no air friction.

questions.question: Pick the correct statement among the following.

options.a: The effort is applied between the fulcrum and the load in class II levers.
options.b: The single fixed pulley helps us to multiply force.
options.c: The M.A. of class II levers is more than one.
options.d: Sugar tongs are an example of class II levers.

questions.solution: (c) The M.A. of class II levers is more than one, since the effort arm is always longer than the load arm. (In class II the load, not the effort, is between fulcrum and effort; a single fixed pulley only changes direction; sugar tongs are class III.)

questions.chapter: Force: Turning Forces and Uniform Circular Motion
questions.topic: Weight of half-metre scale by moments
questions.question:
Find the weight of the given half meter scale.
(Figure: a uniform half-metre scale pivoted at the 15 cm mark, with a weight of 35 gf hanging at its 0 cm end; the scale is balanced.)
questions.solution: (a) 52.5 gf. C.G. of the half-metre scale is at 25 cm. Moments about the 15 cm pivot: 35 × 15 = W × (25 − 15) → W = 525/10 = 52.5 gf.

questions.topic: Path of ray through rectangular glass slab
questions.question: The path of a ray of light coming from air and passing through a rectangular glass slab is traced by four students as shown in the figure - (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv). Which one of them is correct?
questions.solution: (a) (ii). The ray bends towards the normal on entering the glass and away from the normal on leaving it, so the emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray but laterally displaced — as in (ii).
questions.figure_desc: Four rectangular glass slabs (i)-(iv) each with a ray traced through it: (i) straight undeviated, (ii) bends towards normal inside and emerges parallel to incident ray, (iii) bends only on emerging, (iv) bends on entry and continues without bending at exit.

questions.topic: Meaning of power of a lens
questions.question: What does the power of a lens measure?
questions.solution: (b) Deviation of ray of light. The power of a lens is a measure of the deviating (converging or diverging) ability of the lens on the rays refracted through it; P = 1/f.

questions.question: The graph of voltage v/s current for 4 different materials is shown below. Which of these four materials would be used for making the coil of a toaster?
questions.solution: (c) P. Slope of the V–I graph gives resistance; P has the steepest slope and hence the highest resistance (resistivity), which suits a heating element.

questions.question: Two blocks P and Q of different metals having their masses in the ratio 3 : 2 are given the same amount of heat. Their temperature rises by the same amount. Find the ratio of their specific heat capacities.
questions.solution: (c) 2 : 3. Q = mcΔT with same Q and ΔT gives c ∝ 1/m, so cP : cQ = 2 : 3.

questions.question: Which of the following radiations suffer maximum deflection in a magnetic field?
questions.solution: (b) Beta radiations. Beta particles are very light charged particles, so they are deflected the most; alpha are heavy (less deflection) and gamma/X-rays are uncharged (no deflection).

questions.topic: Consequences of high specific heat of water
questions.question:
From the given below applications, select the natural phenomena and consequences of high specific heat capacity of water
(i) Hot water bottles are used as fomentation.
(ii) Farmers fill their fields with water to protect the crops from frost.
(iii) Snow on mountains does not melt all at once.
(iv) When ice in a frozen lake starts melting, its surrounding becomes very cold.
questions.solution: (c) Both (i) and (ii). Hot water bottles and flooding fields against frost use the high specific heat capacity of water; (iii) and (iv) are due to the high specific latent heat of fusion of ice.

questions.topic: Ice cools better than water at 0 °C
concepts: latent heat of fusion of ice
questions.question: Soft drinks are more effectively cooled by ice cubes than by water at 0 °C. Explain.
questions.solution: Ice at 0 °C first absorbs a large amount of latent heat (336 J per gram) from the drink to melt into water at 0 °C, without any rise in its own temperature; only after that does it absorb heat as water. Water at 0 °C can absorb only its sensible heat. Hence ice extracts much more heat and cools the drink more effectively.

marking_points.point: Ice absorbs latent heat of fusion (336 J/g) while melting
Hence absorbs more heat than water at 0 °C, cooling better

questions.question: All stringed musical instruments are provided with a large and hollow sound box. What kind of sound is heard from this sound box and why?
questions.solution: A loud sound is heard. The vibrating strings cause forced vibrations of the sound box and the large mass of air inside it; the air in the box resonates (its natural frequency matches), so a large area/volume of air vibrates and the sound becomes louder (greater amplitude).

marking_points.point: Forced vibrations/resonance of the air in the box; larger vibrating area

questions.question:
Calculate the resistance between terminals P and Q.
(Network: a rectangle with P at the bottom-left corner and Q at the top-right corner. Left side 3 Ω, top side 2 Ω, right side 3 Ω, bottom side 2 Ω, and a 1 Ω resistor along the diagonal directly joining P and Q.)
questions.solution:
Between P and Q there are three parallel paths: left 3 Ω + top 2 Ω = 5 Ω; bottom 2 Ω + right 3 Ω = 5 Ω; diagonal 1 Ω.
1/R = 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/1 = 7/5 → R = 5/7 Ω ≈ 0.71 Ω.

marking_points.point: Identifying three parallel paths of 5 Ω, 5 Ω and 1 Ω

questions.topic: Useful power and electric power via efficiency
questions.question: A machine is used to lift a 100 kg stone to a vertical height 20 m in 80 s. Find the useful power of the machine. If the efficiency of the machine is 75%, find the electric power of the machine. (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.solution:
Useful work = mgh = 100 × 10 × 20 = 20000 J. Useful power = 20000/80 = 250 W.
Efficiency = output power/input power → input (electric) power = 250/0.75 = 333.3 W.

questions.topic: Hazard of interchanged live and neutral
concepts: switch and fuse in live wire
questions.question: Mr. Das calls an electrician to fix a power outage. The electrician interchanges the live and neutral wires in the socket. The appliances still work. What hazards could Mr. Das and his family face in this situation even though the circuit is complete?
questions.solution: The switch and fuse are then in the neutral wire. Even when the switch is off (or the fuse blows), the appliance remains connected to the live wire, so touching it while repairing/cleaning can give a severe electric shock. Also, in case of a short circuit/overload the fuse in the neutral line will not cut off the live supply, risking fire.

marking_points.point: Switch/fuse come in neutral line, so appliance stays live even when switched off
Risk of electric shock / fuse fails to protect against short circuit or fire

questions.question: Raj performed an experiment using two glass slabs A and B of equal thickness but having different refractive indices. Which glass slab will produce a greater lateral displacement of the light ray and why?
questions.solution: The slab with the higher refractive index produces greater lateral displacement. For the same thickness and angle of incidence, a higher refractive index bends the ray more towards the normal inside the slab, so the emergent ray is shifted more.

marking_points.point: Reason: more bending towards normal → greater lateral shift (same thickness)

questions.question: Two copper wires A and B are of the same thickness and are at the room temperature. If the length of A is twice the length of B, then (a) Compare their resistances and (b) their resistivity.
questions.solution:
(a) R ∝ l for the same material and thickness, so RA : RB = 2 : 1.
(b) Resistivity depends only on the material and temperature, so ρA : ρB = 1 : 1.

questions.question: An electric heater draws 5 A of current for 10 minutes when connected to 230 V power supply. Find the heat energy supplied.
An electric gadget can give an electric shock to its user under certain circumstances. Mention any of these two circumstances.

1. When the live wire touches the metallic body of the gadget due to faulty/worn-out insulation and the body is not earthed.
2. When the switch is connected in the neutral wire, or the gadget is handled with wet hands/while standing on a wet floor.

marking_points.point: Live wire touching unearthed metal body (faulty insulation)
Switch in neutral / wet hands etc.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Total internal reflection in a right-angled prism
questions.question:
The critical angle of the material of the given prism below is 42°. Copy and complete the path of the incident ray till the light ray emerges out.
(Figure: a right-angled prism with angles 30° at the top, 60° at the bottom-left and 90° at the bottom-right; a ray enters normally (vertically upward) through the horizontal base.)
questions.solution: The ray enters the base normally and goes straight up undeviated to the slanting face (hypotenuse). There the angle of incidence is 60°, which is greater than the critical angle 42°, so the ray is totally internally reflected. The reflected ray travels towards the vertical face, making an angle of incidence of 30° (< 42°) with its normal, so it refracts out into air bending away from the normal (angle of refraction ≈ 48°, since μ = 1/sin 42° ≈ 1.5 and sin r = 1.5 × sin 30° ≈ 0.75).

marking_points.point: i = 60° at hypotenuse, > 42°, total internal reflection drawn
Emerges from vertical face with i = 30°, bending away from normal

questions.figure_desc: Right-angled prism (30° top, 60° bottom-left, 90° bottom-right) with a ray incident normally on the base from below.

questions.topic: Convex lens as magnifier: v and f
questions.question:
A convex lens forms an image 16 cm long of an object 4 cm long kept at a distance 6 cm from the lens. The object and the image are on the same side of the lens.
(a) What is the nature of the image?
(b) Find the position of the image and (c) the focal length of the lens.
questions.solution:
(a) Virtual, erect and magnified (same side as object).
(b) m = I/O = +16/4 = +4 = v/u; u = −6 cm → v = −24 cm, i.e. 24 cm from the lens on the same side as the object.
(c) 1/f = 1/v − 1/u = 1/(−24) − 1/(−6) = −1/24 + 4/24 = 3/24 → f = +8 cm.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
The diagram below shows three resistors connected across a cell of e.m.f. 1.8 V and internal resistance r. Calculate:
(a) Current through 3 Ω resistor
(b) The internal resistance r.
(Circuit: 3 Ω and 1.5 Ω resistors in parallel, this combination in series with a 4 Ω resistor, a key and the cell (1.8 V, r); current in the main circuit is 0.3 A.)
questions.solution:
Parallel combination: 1/Rp = 1/3 + 1/1.5 = 1 → Rp = 1 Ω. External resistance = 1 + 4 = 5 Ω.
(a) P.d. across the parallel part = 0.3 × 1 = 0.3 V; current through 3 Ω = 0.3/3 = 0.1 A.
(b) ε = I(R + r): 1.8 = 0.3(5 + r) → 5 + r = 6 → r = 1 Ω.

questions.topic: Centre of gravity and stability of a block tower
questions.question:
In the given diagram a man is making a tower of wooden blocks by keeping one block over other.
(a) How is the man able to make this balance of all blocks?
(b) Define the concept used in making the balance of all blocks.
(c) Is there any role of mass and shape in making the balance of these wooden blocks?
questions.solution:
(a) He places the blocks so that the vertical line through the combined centre of gravity of the blocks above any level always falls within the base of support below; then the tower stays balanced.
(b) Centre of gravity: the point through which the entire weight of a body acts, whatever its orientation.
(c) Yes. The position of the centre of gravity depends on the distribution of mass and on the shape of the body, so both affect the balance.

marking_points.point: (a) Keeps C.G. vertically over the base of support
(c) Yes – C.G. depends on mass distribution and shape

questions.topic: Magnifying glass: thickness and focal length
questions.question:
Read the case given below and answer the questions that follow:
Raju's uncle asked Raju to bring a magnifying glass to read the newspaper. Raju brings three glasses of different thickness and Raju's uncle picks up the thickest glass.
(a) What kind of lens is the magnifying glass?
(b) Why did Raju's uncle select the thickest glass?
(c) Name the method that Raju will use to find the focal length of the lens?
questions.solution:
(a) Convex (converging) lens.
(b) The thickest lens has the shortest focal length (greatest power), so it gives the greatest magnification.
(c) The distant object method: focus the image of a distant object (e.g. a far-off tree/sun) on a screen; the distance between the lens and the screen is the focal length.

marking_points.point: (b) Thicker lens → shorter focal length → more magnification

questions.topic: Resonance in pendulum-like wires of different lengths
questions.question:
The adjacent diagram shows four solid plastic balls with wires fitted on a wooden base. A person shakes the wooden base to and fro (forward and backward) periodically. It is observed that even the balls start vibrating. It is also observed that all balls vibrate, but only one ball vibrates vigorously.
(a) Why only one ball vibrates vigorously? (only 1 sentence)
(b) If fA, fB, fC and fD are the natural frequencies of vibration of the wires, then arrange them in the increasing order of their frequencies and give reasons for the same.
(Figure: four vertical wires on a wooden base with balls at their tops; heights in decreasing order D > A > C > B.)
questions.solution:
(a) The ball whose natural frequency equals the frequency of shaking of the base is in resonance, so it vibrates with maximum amplitude.
(b) fD < fA < fC < fB. The natural frequency of a wire decreases as its length increases; D is the longest and B the shortest.

marking_points.point: (a) Resonance – natural frequency equals frequency of shaking
(b) Reason: longer wire → lower natural frequency

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Study the given below graph, answer the following questions:
(Graph: energy (y-axis) vs height above the ground (x-axis). Line C is horizontal; line A rises from the origin; line B falls from the top-left to zero at the right; A and B cross at point O.)
(a) What is indicated by graph line B?
(b) What correlation do you find between lines A and B?
(c) What conclusion can be drawn from point O?
questions.solution:
(a) Line B shows the kinetic energy of the body, which decreases as the height above the ground increases.
(b) A (potential energy) increases with height exactly as B (kinetic energy) decreases, so their sum (line C, total mechanical energy) remains constant — conservation of mechanical energy.
(c) At O, kinetic energy = potential energy = half the total mechanical energy; this happens at half the maximum height.

marking_points.point: (b) PE increases as KE decreases; sum constant (C)
(c) At O, KE = PE = half of total energy (mid-height)

questions.figure_desc: Energy vs height-above-ground graph: horizontal line C (total energy), rising line A (PE) and falling line B (KE) crossing at point O.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Mixture of ice and liquid: final temperature
questions.question: 50 g of ice at 0 °C is added to 300 g of a liquid at 30 °C. What will be the final temperature of the mixture when all the ice has melted? The specific heat capacity of the liquid is 2.65 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹ while that of water is 4.2 J g⁻¹ °C⁻¹, specific latent heat of fusion of ice = 336 J g⁻¹.
questions.solution:
Let final temperature be T.
Heat gained by ice = 50 × 336 + 50 × 4.2 × T = 16800 + 210T.
Heat lost by liquid = 300 × 2.65 × (30 − T) = 795(30 − T) = 23850 − 795T.
Heat gained = heat lost: 16800 + 210T = 23850 − 795T → 1005T = 7050 → T ≈ 7.0 °C.

questions.topic: Fissionability of uranium isotopes; alpha decay equation
questions.question:
The ore of uranium found in nature contains ²³⁸₉₂U and ²³⁵₉₂U. Although both the isotopes are fissionable, it is found out experimentally that one of the isotopes is more easily fissionable.
(a) Name the isotope of uranium which is easily fissionable.
(b) Give a reason for your answer.
(c) Write a nuclear reaction when uranium 238 emits an alpha particle to form a Thorium (Th) nucleus.
[The paper prints the second isotope as ²³⁵₉₀U, a misprint for ²³⁵₉₂U.]
questions.solution:
(a) Uranium-235 (²³⁵₉₂U).
(b) U-235 can be split by slow (thermal) neutrons; it has an odd number of neutrons (143), so absorbing a neutron releases enough energy to cause fission, whereas U-238 needs fast, high-energy neutrons (and usually captures slow ones without fission).
(c) ²³⁸₉₂U → ²³⁴₉₀Th + ⁴₂He (+ energy).

marking_points.point: (b) Fissionable by slow neutrons (U-238 needs fast neutrons)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: Write two differences between nuclear fission and fusion.
questions.solution:
1. Fission: a heavy nucleus splits into two lighter nuclei; fusion: two light nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus.
2. Fission can take place at ordinary temperature by neutron bombardment and produces radioactive waste; fusion requires very high temperature (~10⁷ K) and pressure and produces little/no radioactive waste.

marking_points.point: Splitting heavy nucleus vs combining light nuclei
